Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM` calls `doTest("b:foo/test", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "/b:foo[1]/test[1]")`, which probably involves querying a DOM structure with namespaces. The current bug report describes a problem when requesting `.asPath()` on a node that resets the default namespace causing an endless loop.

Inspecting `NodePointer.asPath()`, the method builds a string path representation recursively, calling `.asPath()` on its parent pointers and appending its own segment. This method can enter a loop if the parent-child relationship or container logic is flawed.

In this method:
- It first checks if the parent is a container (`parent.isContainer()`) and if so, returns the parent's path directly.
- Otherwise, it calls `parent.asPath()` recursively and then appends its own name or attribute info.

The `isContainer()` method in `NodePointer` by default returns `false`, so likely subclass(es) override it. If there's a problem with namespace resetting that causes parent-child links or container status to be inconsistent, calling `.asPath()` can repeatedly call the same methods on nodes in a cycle, causing an endless loop.

The bug report's XML snippet indicates a node `<test xmlns="">` inside a parent that has a default namespace defined (`xmlns="test111"`). This "reset" of the default namespace to empty can confuse namespace handling in the model. Since `getName()` returns a `QName` built from prefix and local name, improper namespace handling might cause ambiguous or malformed parent-child relationships or container flags.

Therefore, the likely root cause is that namespace resetting (empty default namespace) causes the parent/child or container relationships in the model nodes to be inconsistent or cyclic, which leads `NodePointer.asPath()` to recursively call itself infinitely.

Additional detailed inspection of namespace handling in node pointer generation and container determination methods would be needed to fix this issue.

Summary: The endless loop is caused by incorrect handling of nodes with a reset default namespace, leading to cyclic or inconsistent parent/child or container relationships. This makes the recursive `NodePointer.asPath()` call enter an infinite recursion.

Next, I'll locate potential methods related to namespace handling in node pointers that could be responsible.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
